titleZh: 酒店发消费券，到底赚不赚钱？先算清这四笔账
titleEn: Do Hotel Vouchers Really Make Money? Check These Four Numbers First
summaryZh: 消费券核销快不等于酒店赚钱。先核对补贴到账、酒店让利、额外成本和正价订单是否被挤掉，再决定是否扩大。
summaryEn: Fast voucher redemption does not equal hotel profit. Check subsidy settlement, hotel-funded discounts, extra costs and displaced full-rate demand before scaling.
contentZh:
# 酒店发消费券，到底赚不赚钱？先算清这四笔账

券核销快不等于赚。消费券带来的订单增长和利润增长是两回事。判断要不要扩大发券，先看四笔账：补贴实际到账、酒店让利、额外成本、正价订单是否被挤掉。

第一笔账是补贴实际到账。北京市石景山区2026年第二期住宿餐饮消费券住宿核销期为9月5日至10月17日，住宿满300减75、满400减100、满600减150，住宿券14天为一个周期，单笔最多一张。该活动只能说明当地存在具体促消费安排，不能推出全国酒店收益结论。酒店必须确认补贴由谁承担、是否全额返还、何时到账、是否影响发票和账务处理。补贴没有实际到账，就不能计入真实收益。

第二笔账是酒店让利。要算清没有消费券时这单原本能卖多少钱，券下单价是否低于正常可售价格，让利是否超过补贴净收益。如果只是把正价订单换成低价订单，酒店没有新增利润。

第三笔账是额外成本。前台核销、客服解释、退改、对账、发票、平台服务费、培训和差错都要计入，不能只看订单金额。

第四笔账是正价订单是否被挤掉。要看同期正价订单、平均房价、取消率、高价时段占用和客群结构。正价订单被挤掉，消费券越成功，酒店越亏。

不要一开始就全渠道、全房型、全时段发券。先做两周小规模测试，选择部分房型、日期和渠道。财务确认结算口径，收益负责人监控正价订单与平均房价，总经理控制执行压力，业主确认让利和现金流影响。

出现正价订单减少、平均房价下降、补贴结算延迟、核销失败率上升、退订投诉增加、额外成本超过补贴净收益或财务无法对账，应立即停止或缩小规模。消费券更适合淡季、工作日和明显空置库存，不适合旺季、周末、会议期和正价订单充足的时段。

明天第一步：让财务确认补贴到账口径，让收益负责人调出同期正价订单数据，让总经理评估执行能力，让业主确认让利由谁承担。四笔账算清之前，只做最小测试，不做扩张决定。
contentEn:
# Do Hotel Vouchers Really Make Money? Check These Four Numbers First

Fast voucher redemption does not equal hotel profit. More voucher orders and more profit are two different things. Before expanding a voucher programme, check four numbers: subsidy actually received, discount funded by the hotel, incremental cost, and full-rate demand displaced by voucher bookings.

First, verify the subsidy settlement. Beijing’s Shijingshan District published a second-round accommodation and dining voucher programme for 2026. Accommodation vouchers are redeemable from 5 September to 17 October, with offers of RMB 75 off RMB 300, RMB 100 off RMB 400, and RMB 150 off RMB 600. One voucher may be used per order, with a 14-day cycle. This proves that a local promotion exists; it does not prove a national hotel profit result. Confirm who funds the subsidy, whether the full amount is reimbursed, when it settles, and how it affects invoicing and accounting. Until the money is actually received, do not count it as real profit.

Second, calculate the hotel-funded discount. What would this booking have sold for without the voucher? Is the voucher price below the normal sellable price? Is the hotel’s contribution greater than the net subsidy? If a voucher merely converts a full-rate booking into a discounted booking, it has not created incremental profit.

Third, include incremental cost. Front-desk redemption, guest explanations, changes and cancellations, reconciliation, invoicing, platform fees, training and error handling all consume resources. A hotel that counts only room revenue will overstate the result.

Fourth, test whether full-rate demand has been displaced. Track full-rate bookings, average room rate, cancellation, high-value dates and customer mix. If voucher bookings occupy rooms that would have sold at full rate, the more successful the voucher looks, the worse the hotel may perform.

Do not open every room type, channel and date at once. Run a two-week minimum test on selected inventory. Finance confirms settlement; revenue management tracks full-rate demand and average rate; the general manager controls execution pressure; the owner confirms who absorbs the discount and the cash-flow impact.

Stop or reduce the programme if full-rate bookings fall, average rate declines, settlement is delayed, redemption errors rise, cancellations and complaints increase, incremental cost exceeds net subsidy, or finance cannot reconcile the bookings. Vouchers are more suitable for soft weekdays and clearly empty inventory than for peak dates, weekends, meetings or periods with strong full-rate demand.

Tomorrow’s first move is simple: confirm the settlement rule, pull comparable full-rate booking data, assess execution capacity and identify who funds the discount. Until the four numbers are clear, run only the smallest test. Do not scale.
author: 迈创兄弟C&T（MarvelBros C&T）
